answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08 these proteins are not unrelated. They share class b (All beta proteins), fold b.6 (Cupredoxin-like) and superfamily b.6.1 (Cupredoxins). SCOPe places them in different families within that superfamily: plastocyanin/azurin-like is b.6.1.1 (sunid 49504), ephrin ectodomain is b.6.1.5 (sunid 74874, e.g. Ephrin-B2 ectodomain and Ephrin-A5 proteins), and Peptidylarginine deiminase Pad4 N-terminal domain is b.6.1.6 (sunid 110107, e.g. d5n0ya1). Other families in b.6.1 include cytochrome c oxidase subunit II periplasmic domain (b.6.1.2), multidomain cupredoxins (b.6.1.3), nitrosocyanin (b.6.1.4) and SO1698-like (b.6.1.7). The lowest shared level is therefore the superfamily, and SCOPe superfamily membership is its evidence-based call for a probable common evolutionary origin. That relationship is distant and structure-based. They are not in the same family, so close sequence-level relatedness is not implied. The conserved cupredoxin-like beta-sandwich (Greek-key) scaffold has been co-opted for very different roles. Function should not be transferred. The only copper annotation I found is at the b.6.1 superfamily node, 'contains copper-binding site'. It describes the superfamily as a whole and does not say that every member binds copper. Copper binding and electron transfer are established for plastocyanin/azurin-like members, which have the characteristic Cys/His/His/Met ligand set. Ephrin ectodomains are receptor-binding (Eph receptor ligand) domains and the PAD4 N-terminal domain is part of a calcium-dependent peptidylarginine deiminase. For these two I rely on background knowledge and did not check ligand residues or cofactors in structures. Neither family's SCOPe family-level classification supports a redox or copper role. A shared fold or superfamily is not evidence of shared function, and the copper site is unlikely to be conserved without its ligand residues, so any copper-binding or electron-transfer claim for ephrin or PAD4 would need independent evidence such as conserved ligand residues, bound metal in structures, or biochemical assays. Do not use cupredoxin templates or annotations to assign metal binding or electron transfer to ephrins or PAD4. Treat superfamily membership as a basis for structural comparison only.
evidence_used: pretrained knowledge of cupredoxin copper sites, ephrin and PAD4 biology
